description: Oath and zeal - a melee templar whose strikes call holy fire down on their own.
_source_note: Rebuilt 5 Nov 2026 from the 39 real CoA Zealot talents (role DPS). COMBO IS A REAL PRIMARY RESOURCE for Templar and six abilities generate 20 each, so CoA's Energy talents land on a pool that exists - the first time in this audit a CoA resource system has. Calm Combatant ports exactly (spell damage from attack power is a legal pair). Zealotry builds as a proc with a damage_flat payload, so the spec's signature fires; what is lost is the Oath Chain bookkeeping, since nothing counts how many times a proc fired during a window. Expertise is live again now that creatures have avoidance.

nodes.name: Calm Combatant
nodes.description: Increases your spell damage by 30% of your attack power.
nodes._source: CoA's level 20 passive: 'Increases your Holy spell damage by 30% of your attack power.' PORTS EXACTLY - spell_damage is in STAT_CONVERSION_TARGETS and attack_power is in STAT_CONVERSION_SOURCES (as `ap`), so a melee Templar turning attack power into spell damage is real. The Holy scoping is dropped: there is no per-school damage key, and this spec's spell damage is all Holy anyway. A FRACTION.

nodes.name: Solemn Soldier
nodes.description: Increases your haste by 10% and your expertise by 10.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Increases your melee haste by 5% and expertise by 5.' Doubled for the two ranks. BOTH HALVES PORT, which they would not have earlier today: `expertise` was read by no engine code for most of this audit - it reduces a target's dodge and parry, and monsters had neither - so Guardian's Stalwart and Gladiator's Double Duty both had to drop it. Kyle had creature avoidance added on 5 Nov 2026 (dodge on every template, parry on humanoids), which made expertise a real stat, and the two Guardian nodes were restored. It is in PERCENTAGE POINTS and subtracts from the target's dodge AND parry independently.

nodes.name: Martial Paladin
nodes.description: Increases your Agility by 10% and your chance to hit by 6%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Increases your Agility by 5% and your chance to hit by 3%.' Doubled for the two ranks. agility_pct takes percentage POINTS and hit_rating is a PERCENT - the two happen to read the same way here. Note hit and expertise are NOT duplicates: hit beats the attacker-side roll, expertise strips the target's avoidance, and they are separate checks.

nodes.name: Bursting Impact
nodes.description: Increases your physical damage by 25%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases your off-hand weapon damage by 25%.' THERE IS NO OFF-HAND DAMAGE KEY - the engine does not model main and off hand separately for talent purposes - so it lands on physical damage generally. Broader than CoA's, stated rather than hidden; CoA's version only pays a dual-wielding Templar, and this one pays any.

nodes.name: Radiance
nodes.description: Reduces the cost of Vindication by 20%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Reduces the Energy cost of Vindication by -5.' CoA's Templar spends Energy; Frontier's spends COMBO, which is a real primary resource with six abilities generating 20 each - so there IS a cost to reduce. A flat 5 is expressed as a percentage because costs differ per rank. POSITIVE reduces.

nodes.name: Combat Training
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Vindication by 20%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases the effectiveness of Oaths by 20%.' AN OATH IS NOT A THING HERE - CoA's Vindication 'grants an Oath', Oaths give damaging abilities a 10% chance to trigger Zealotry, and nothing in this engine holds that kind of stacking charge that other abilities read. Re-pointed at Vindication, the ability that granted the Oath, which is the nearest live thing.

nodes.name: Zealotry
nodes.description: Your strikes have a 20% chance to call down holy fire.
nodes._source: CoA's signature mechanic: 'Oath: Your damaging abilities have a 10% chance to trigger Zealotry. Zealotry deals 40% off-hand Weapon Damage as Holy Damage.' ZEALOTRY ITSELF PORTS CLEANLY - a proc with a damage_flat payload and a school is exactly its shape. The chance is doubled to 20% because CoA's 10% is conditional on holding an Oath and this is not. The damage is flat rather than a share of off-hand weapon damage, since a payload cannot read weapon damage. Eight other talents in this tree read Zealotry and most of them work off this node.

nodes.name: Blade Sermon
nodes.description: Increases all damage you deal by 10%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Increases the Weapon Damage dealt by Zealotry by 10%.' Zealotry is a PROC PAYLOAD here, not an ability, so there is no ability_*_damage key for it - and no key scales a proc's damage_flat. Doubled for the two ranks and applied as all_damage, which does reach the proc's payload through the normal damage path.

nodes.name: Priest Training
nodes.description: Your strikes that call holy fire also heal you.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Triggering Zealotry now also heals you for 3% of your missing health.' A proc cannot read another proc firing, so this is a second proc on the same trigger and chance as Zealotry - they fire together in practice, which is what CoA describes. heal_flat is flat because no payload reads a percentage of missing health; 1-turn icd so a multi-hit turn does not stack the heals.

nodes.name: Chakra of Power
nodes.description: Your critical strikes restore 10 combo.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Melee attacks now restore 1 Energy, plus an additional 2 Energy when they critically strike.' Templar's resource is COMBO, so there is a real pool to grant into - verified by six abilities carrying `generates` blocks for 20 combo. Built on the crit half only: on_weapon_swing would fire every turn for 1 combo, which rounds to noise against a 20-combo generator. 10 on a crit is the same throughput, concentrated.

nodes.name: Upheave!
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike damage of Righteous Upheaval by 20%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases the critical damage of Righteous Upheaval by 20%.' Ports exactly. ability_*_crit_damage is a FRACTION, unlike ability_*_crit which is a PERCENT.

nodes.name: Battle Hardened
nodes.description: Reduces the cooldown of Righteous Upheaval by 25%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Reduces the cooldown of Righteous Upheaval by 5 sec.' Expressed as a percentage against the ability's own 20-second cooldown. POSITIVE reduces.

nodes.name: Holy Upheaval
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Righteous Upheaval by 50%.
nodes._source: CoA's level 30 passive: 'Increases the effectiveness Righteous Upheaval gains per trigger of Zealotry by 100%.' THIS IS THE NODE THAT MOST WANTS THE OATH CHAIN AND CANNOT HAVE IT. CoA's Righteous Upheaval is 'increased by 3% for each time you triggered Zealotry during your Oath Chain', and nothing counts how many times a proc fired during a window - no key reads a proc's history, and no effect holds a tally other abilities can read. Doubling that scaling therefore has nothing to double. Granted as flat damage at roughly what a good chain would have reached.

nodes.name: Deliverance
nodes.description: Your critical strikes with Vindication or Righteous Lunge strike again for physical damage.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Critically striking with Vindication or Righteous Lunge now deals 50% additional Physical damage.' bonus_pct would be the exact translation - it adds a share of the triggering hit - but it is reserved here for a flat second strike so the node reads distinctly from Pyromancer Draconic's Aspect of Time. Both of CoA's abilities exist and the filter is exact.

nodes.name: Iron Penance
nodes.description: Your strikes leave the enemy taking 1% more physical damage per stack for 1 turn, stacking 10 times.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Dealing damage with Zealotry now applies Iron Penance to the target, increasing their Physical damage taken by you by 1% for 3 seconds, stacking 10 times.' A proc cannot read another proc firing, so it hangs off the same builders Zealotry does. CoA's 1% and 10 stacks kept; 3 seconds is 1 turn, which makes the ramp genuinely hard to hold - as CoA's short window intends. The 'by you' scoping has no key; it is a general debuff. INSIDE A STATUS EFFECT physical_damage_taken_pct is divided by 100 and POSITIVE INCREASES damage taken.

nodes.name: Condemnation
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike chance of Condemn by 10%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases the critical strike chance gained through Condemn by 3%.' CoA's Condemn grants crit as a buff; nothing here reads that, so the crit is applied to Condemn itself. Raised to 10% since it now only affects one ability rather than everything after it.

nodes.name: One-Punch Man
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Righteous Upheaval and Titanstrike by 20%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases the damage of Oath Breakers and Titanstrike by 20%.' CoA's 'Oath Breakers' is its term for the finishers; Righteous Upheaval is the one Frontier has, and Titanstrike exists by name. CoA's 20% kept.

nodes.name: Pious Sweep
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Chastise by 25%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases the damage of Chastise by 25% on enemies above 75% health or affected by Tranquil Circle.' NEITHER CONDITION CAN BE READ - no effect key reads a target's health percentage or its debuffs - so CoA's 25% applies always. Chastise exists in Frontier.

nodes.name: Libram of Zeal
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Libram of Zeal by 40% and reduces its cooldown by 25%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Read from your Libram of Mortal Abdication, increasing your melee haste by 20% and causes your damaging abilities to reduce the cooldown of Righteous Upheaval by 2 sec for 20 sec. Only 1 Libram spell can be active at a time.' Frontier HAS Libram of Zeal as an ability and it is NOT gated, so this is not its unlock. The 'only 1 Libram active' rule has no exclusive-group mechanism available to a talent, and the cooldown-feeding rider would need a second proc. Built as damage and cooldown on the ability itself.

nodes.name: Chakra of Light
nodes.description: Reduces the cooldown of your Testaments by 30%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Reduces the cooldown of Testaments by 30 sec and Oath Breakers now heal allies around the target.' All five Testaments are written out because no key names a group - Fortitude, Will, Faith, Hope and Strength. The ally-healing half is dropped: a talent cannot make an ability heal allies it does not already heal. 30 sec is expressed as 30% of their own cooldowns.

nodes.name: Light's Guidance
nodes.description: Increases the healing of Benediction by 50%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim for both halves: 'Healing with Benediction now causes your next Benediction to heal for 25% more for 30 seconds' and, from Holy Light, 'Your Benediction now has a 1.5 sec cast time, but now heals for 100% more.' Nothing empowers a named next cast, and there are no cast times to trade away. The two are merged into one flat 50% - between CoA's 25% stacking and its 100% with a cast-time penalty that cannot be charged.

nodes.name: Heaven's Finest
nodes.description: Your strikes build zeal, restoring 4 combo per stack for 4 turns, stacking 6 times.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Damaging abilities now grant Heaven's Finest for 12 sec, stacking 6 times. Increases your movement speed by 5%. At 6 stacks, increases your Energy regeneration by 100% for 8 sec.' Movement speed is positional, the 6-stack threshold cannot be read, and THERE IS NO RESOURCE REGENERATION KEY. Rebuilt as a direct combo grant on every builder - which is what doubled regeneration delivered, paid out per strike instead of at a threshold. The description states the stacking shape CoA describes even though the grant is flat per cast.

nodes.name: Force of Golganneth
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Force of Golganneth by 50% and reduces the cost of Temple Guardian by 50%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Explode with holy power, dealing Holy damage and triggering Zealotry every 0.5 sec to nearby enemies for 5 sec. While active, your Temple Guardian spell has its Energy cost reduced by 50%.' Frontier HAS Force of Golganneth and it is not gated. The repeated Zealotry triggers need a periodic trigger, which does not exist, and the 'while active' gate has no key - so the cost reduction is permanent at CoA's own 50%. Temple Guardian is target_type 'party', so making it cheaper is real party value.

nodes.name: Divine Fury
nodes.description: Increases your critical strike chance by 8% and your critical strike damage by 20%.
nodes._source: CoA's own description for this node is the unresolved token '$64' - the Builder payload never expands it - so there is no verbatim text and this is NOT a faithful copy. Frontier HAS Divine Fury as an ability and it is not gated, so this cannot be its unlock either. Named from CoA's own title and built as crit, which every node around it feeds. Flagged so a later pass can correct it. TWO UNITS IN ONE BLOCK: crit_chance_physical is a PERCENT, crit_damage_physical a FRACTION.

nodes.name: Norgannon's Wrath
nodes.description: Teaches Norgannon's Wrath, and your holy fire strikes twice as hard.
nodes._source: LOAD-BEARING UNLOCK: templar_norgannons_wrath carries requires_talent, so without this node it is unobtainable forever. Templar has exactly three gated abilities, one per tree - this one, Oathkeeper's Tome of Light and Crusader's Righteous Tempest - and main() asserts this one. The all_damage is added because a capstone granting only an ability is thin, and because all_damage is the one key that reaches Zealotry's proc payload (see Blade Sermon), so the capstone really does make the holy fire hit harder rather than just claiming to.
